answer: A strong Sybil defense is a stake-and-slash vault: every agent must lock a meaningful deposit before it can earn, and the deposit is slashed if the agent is caught duplicating identities or spamming fake work. At the zenith of its reputation, an agent that has behaved honestly for months unlocks higher rewards, while a fresh clone starts at zero and cannot harvest the nectar of the network — paid tasks, referrals, and trust — without first risking real capital and time. Attackers then face a simple math problem: each fake identity costs more to create than it can ever earn back.
